ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus himalayanus* reaches 70 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal bands and possesses slender, curved digits and a distinctively tuberculate dorsal surface.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus himalayanus* is best distinguished by its unique dorsal pattern of 4–5 dark, irregular transverse bands that are typically narrower than the pale interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus himalayanus* inhabits moist temperate forests and rocky outcrops in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Himalayan Bent-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dusk to actively forage for small insects and invertebrates across rocky terrain and forest surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus himalayanus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus himalayanus* is found in the Himalayan foothills of India, specifically in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
